goal: Phase 2a diet (docs/intent-factory/TECH-SPEC-2026-09-05-lean.md, revision 5, section 3 rule 3 and section 5 row 2a). Delete every spend ceiling from intent-factory: contract schema 3 has no maxInputTokens, maxCostUsd, usagePolicy or budgetProfile, and no progressPolicy with its file-change watchdog; budget.mjs, capsule.mjs, the usage ledger with its epochs and judge reserve, budget continuation segments and cache-read session rotation go with their tests. Usage stays recorded per invocation in <run-dir>/usage.jsonl for reporting only, and status, report, metrics and the dashboard read it. Time (timeoutSec, stallTimeoutSec) and the provider's own allowance (rule 8) are the only limits. Owner decision of 2026-09-07 (no-spend-ceiling): ceilings in USD or tokens deliver no value and have interrupted several campaigns; two phase failures of this campaign were budget_exceeded and none was real overspend. Take 2: take 1 ran on deepseek-v4-pro until the provider answered 402 Insufficient Balance after forty minutes; its partial diet (22 files, 266 insertions, 4664 deletions) is checkpoint a1370ac on campaign/lean-v03 and this take finishes it on claude-sonnet-5 with no judge, because DeepSeek was the only cross-vendor judge left and a same-vendor judge is forbidden; the full suite is the gate.

definitionOfDone.text: Contract schema 3 has no spend ceiling: maxInputTokens, maxCostUsd, usagePolicy, budgetProfile and progressPolicy are rejected by validation at contract and node level with an error naming the field, and budget.mjs, capsule.mjs, the usage ledger with its epochs and lock, the judge reserve, budget continuation segments, cache-read session rotation with its capsule handoff, and the file-change progress watchdog with its dry heartbeats are deleted together with their tests and their reference documentation; observable in scripts/contract.mjs, the deleted files, test/contract.test.mjs and references/contract.md.

Every worker and judge invocation appends one record to <run-dir>/usage.jsonl — node, attempt, role, runtime id and model, tokens by kind (uncached input, cache read, output), cost with provenance (provider-reported, priced or unknown), started and finished timestamps — and nothing reads it for control; status, report, metrics and the dashboard read usage.jsonl and node state instead of the ledger and show raw tokens by kind and cost, never weighted input, remaining budget or judge reserve; observable in a usage.jsonl written by the replay tests and in the metrics, dashboard, statusline and render tests.

An attempt ends only by completion, timeoutSec, stallTimeoutSec, cancellation or a provider exhaustion handled by rule 8 (exhaustedUntil, same-tier re-tier, attention); every budget_exceeded path, the resume --max-input-tokens extension, the rotation handoff and the `handoff` command are gone. Provider session continuation (rule 4) is kept in substance: continuationId and the reuse-versus-fresh decision on resume are unchanged, and a fresh continuation prompt is composed from node state — the previous attempt's error, findings and changed-files summary appended as a bounded 'Previous attempt' section — instead of from a capsule. Rule-8 handling is untouched. Observable in scripts/runner.mjs, scripts/failover.mjs and the replay suite.

taskPacket.objective: Remove every spend ceiling and the machinery that enforced it, keep per-invocation usage as a reporting record in usage.jsonl, and leave every reader (status, report, metrics, dashboard, status line) and the full suite green.
instructions: Before you declare the work done, run every command proof in this node's Definition of Done — `npm run check` and `npm run typecheck` — in the foreground and fix what they report. The controller runs them again at the gate and a failure there costs the whole attempt.

Never start a command in the background or through a task tool, and never wait on one with a sleep loop: the tool policy denies background Bash and the controller reads silence as a stall. Bound output with | tail -n 200. You are a headless session: ending your turn ends the session, nobody resumes you, and the controller treats a missing canonical result file as a protocol failure that discards the attempt — never 'pause to wait'; run every command in the foreground with an explicit tool timeout (the Bash tool's timeout parameter, up to 600000 ms) and keep each command under eight minutes: runner.test.mjs only through the three name-pattern splits `--test-name-pattern='^r'`, `'^a'`, `'^[^ar]'`, never the whole file in one command. Never run npm install, npm ci or any package install: the worktree has no node_modules by design (tsc is global), and the husky prepare hook would write .husky/_/.gitignore and fail the node's snapshot-integrity check. The controller rotates a Claude session after 600 observed turns and the rotation loses the worktree's uncommitted edits, so aim to finish well under 500 turns: batch related edits before testing, run whole files or pattern splits instead of many single-test runs, never re-read a range you already read, and run the full five-part suite at most twice.

The controller verifies this node with the full suite in five parts (runner.test.mjs split by test-name pattern ^r, ^a and ^[^ar] so each part fits the 600 s verification ceiling, then skills/mine/intent-factory/test/*.mjs, then test/*.mjs) and a failed verification discards the attempt, so run the same three commands yourself in the foreground before finishing, each with a generous tool timeout (they take several minutes; that is expected): `node --test skills/mine/intent-factory/scripts/runner.test.mjs 2>&1 | tail -n 150`, then `node --test 'skills/mine/intent-factory/test/*.mjs' 2>&1 | tail -n 80`, then `node --test 'test/*.mjs' 2>&1 | tail -n 40`. While iterating, run single files or `--test-name-pattern` selections.

Read docs/intent-factory/TECH-SPEC-2026-09-05-lean.md section 3 (rule 3, rule 8, the module table and the 'Deleted' paragraph) and section 5 row '2a diet' before editing. Node level: maxInputTokens, maxCostUsd, budgetProfile, progressPolicy (graceSec, intervalSec, maxDryHeartbeats) and the dry-heartbeat file-change watchdog that consumes it. Usage for reporting. Tests, each named after its case: schema 3 rejects each deleted field by name at contract and node level and rejects schemaVersion 2 by name; a replay run writes usage.jsonl with one record per worker and judge invocation carrying tokens by kind and cost provenance; metrics reads usage.jsonl and reports tokens by kind; status and report render tokens by kind and cost without weighted input; a replay node whose recorded usage exceeds any former ceiling completes done; timeoutSec still ends an attempt; the existing rule-8 tests are untouched and green; no test references usagePolicy, budgetProfile, progressPolicy or the ledger any more.

The controller running this node is the phase-1 runner from an immutable snapshot under .runs/control, so deleting schema-2 fields from the tree cannot affect this run; the contract you are running under is schema 2 by design. Do not try to keep schema 2 readable — no compatibility layer, no migration, no fallback.

Keep your context small: read by offset or grep, never whole large files. scripts/runner.mjs is over 7700 lines; grep for the symbol, then read a bounded range. Keep SKILL.md under the byte ceiling enforced by test/docs-diet.test.mjs.

Do not modify campaign control artifacts under .runs/control or .runs/campaigns and do not commit. Writing the canonical result file the controller designates is required, and tests may create isolated temporary directories.
decisions: No spend ceiling of any kind survives; time and the provider's own allowance are the limits.
Session rotation is deleted with the capsule: it was a cost control fed by cacheReadWeight, and a worker session now ends only by completion, timeout, stall, cancellation or provider exhaustion.
Usage is recorded per invocation in usage.jsonl for reporting and read by no control path.
Provider session continuation (rule 4) and runtime discovery with re-tiering (rule 8) are untouched.

Do not redesign the dashboard page, the status line layout or the metrics indicators; phases 3 and 4 do that.
